rows.title: Monetary Policy
rows.figure: Fed Dec quarter-point hike ~96% (CME FedWatch via Hercules); RBA Dec hold ~99%, cut ~1% (forex.com); BoC Dec ~80% (Reuters); BoE Dec ~82%; ECB Dec ~90%; BoJ Dec ~84%
rows.read: A December Fed hike is fully priced, so the dollar now needs bets on further hikes to rise much more. Hot Australian inflation ended talk of a cut there, and Canada and the UK still lean toward December hikes. In Japan, mixed inflation signals keep a December hike likely but not certain.

rows.title: Growth
rows.figure: Germany Q3 GDP +0.1% q/q final (first estimate +0.2%, forecast +0.2%) (Destatis); US Q3 GDP second estimate due Wed 7:30 AM CT (forecast 3.5%, advance 3.4%) (Hercules)
rows.read: Germany's economy grew a touch less than first reported in the third quarter, a reminder that its recovery is slow. US growth and spending figures on Wednesday will show whether the US economy is still outrunning the rest, which has kept the dollar strong.

rows.title: Inflation
rows.figure: Australia CPI Oct 4.9% y/y (fcst 4.7%), trimmed mean 3.8% (fcst 3.6%); Japan services PPI Oct +4.2% (fcst 3.6%); BoJ core CPI 2.3% (fcst 2.5%); US core PCE Oct due Wed 7:30 AM CT (fcst +0.3% m/m, 3.2% y/y)
rows.read: Inflation is running hot in Australia and still above target in Japan, which keeps those central banks from easing. US core inflation for October, out Wednesday morning, is the week's biggest test for the dollar.

rows.title: Risk Sentiment
rows.read: Asian markets turned cautious ahead of expected new US tariffs on 16 trading partners. Money went into the dollar this time, while riskier currencies like the Aussie and kiwi fell. Gold slid too, a sign that higher US rates still outweigh fear.

rows.title: Positioning
rows.figure: Hedge funds (CFTC, Nov 17): USD index −1.3K (flipped short), EUR −76.6K, GBP +28.8K, JPY −23.8K, CHF −19.8K, CAD −72.1K, AUD +38.0K, NZD −23.6K; asset managers GBP −104.6K, AUD −182.7K, EUR +147.2K
rows.read: The latest weekly figures show hedge funds have turned slightly against the dollar, while still betting against the euro, the kiwi, the franc and, most strongly, the Canadian dollar. They still bet on the pound and the Aussie, where big long-term investors take the opposite side. Where the two groups disagree, a surprise could set off a fast unwind.

rows.title: Fiscal
rows.figure: USTR Section 301 findings expected soon, 16 partners, final rates not set (Reuters); US 10-year ~4.90% (Hercules, WSJ); S&P France review Fri Nov 27 (Hercules)
rows.read: The US is expected to unveil new tariffs on 16 trading partners, including China, the European Union and Japan, which could weigh on their economies and on US growth. Record US government borrowing keeps long-term US borrowing costs high. France's debts remain a weight on the euro, with S&P due to review its credit rating on Friday.
